\\\ A tuple accumulator cut short by the "maximum function depth" setting.
\\\ The truncated call sums to the polymorphic additive identity rather than
\\\ to the integer 0, so adding it to a tuple stays well-typed and the
\\\ recursion degrades gracefully instead of raising a type error.

set "maximum function depth" to 3

function: recur N:n {
  if N <= 0 { result: [tuple 0 0] }
  result: [tuple 1 1] + [recur N - 1]
}

TRUNCATED: [recur 10]
output TRUNCATED named "truncated tuple"
output [field 1 of TRUNCATED] named "first field"
output [field 2 of TRUNCATED] named "second field"

\\\ A function with no result statement returns an empty dimension-one pool,
\\\ which contributes no outcomes at all rather than summing to zero.
function: maybe X:n { if X > 1 { result: [tuple 7 8] } }
MAYBE: [maybe d2]
output MAYBE named "no-result tuple"
output [field 1 of MAYBE] named "no-result first field"
output [field 2 of MAYBE] named "no-result second field"

\\\ Result \\\

"truncated tuple"
#,#,%
2,2,100

"first field",2,0,2,2
#,%
2,100

"second field",2,0,2,2
#,%
2,100

"no-result tuple"
#,#,%
7,8,100

"no-result first field",7,0,7,7
#,%
7,100

"no-result second field",8,0,8,8
#,%
8,100
